message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I have $935 and am on BOARDWALK. I own five properties but no monopoly. p2 has $1,146. p3 has $1,152. p4 has $427 and one GOOJF card.

I cannot complete any color set without trading. p4 holds two of three light blue properties and needs my Vermont Avenue to finish it. I have two of three pink properties but Virginia is still bank-owned. I own one of three orange properties while Tennessee and New York remain unowned. The utilities are split between us.

I should not trade Vermont Avenue to p4. That would give them a light blue monopoly. I will avoid mortgaging and focus on hunting Virginia, Tennessee, and New York. I cannot trade for Virginia because it is still bank-owned.

A trade for both light blue properties would cost substantial cash. p4 is short on funds and has already rejected dark blue offers. A light blue monopoly with houses is weaker than orange or pink.

A light blue trade would drain too much cash. I need money to buy Virginia, Tennessee, and New York and build houses. I do not have either dark blue property. I am considering a middleman trade for Park Place and Boardwalk.

A dark blue trade is impossible. Fully developing it would cost $2,000, which I do not have.

The yellow and green sets are also unattainable right now.

Completing the pink set is the best remaining path. Virginia would bring me to two of three pink properties. Building three houses on the three pink properties costs about $900. With $935 in cash, I can afford that and still have money left.

Orange is a stronger long-term set than pink. p4 has not yet shown signs of desperation, and they previously declined to trade on light blue or dark blue properties.

Selling Water Works would give p3 a utility monopoly, but utilities are too weak to justify the trade. p2 wants Ventnor from p4.
